input: Research visa requirements for moving to Portugal

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Visa eligibility and categories differ significantly depending on the applicant's nationality — EU citizens have free movement rights while non-EU citizens must apply for specific visas.
Portugal offers many distinct visa types (D7 passive income, Digital Nomad, Golden Visa, D2 entrepreneur, student, etc.) — knowing the intended lifestyle narrows which visa is actually relevant.
The intended move date affects urgency, processing time considerations, and whether certain visa programs currently open or closing (e.g. Golden Visa changes) are still applicable.
The user may want a simple personal summary, a comparison document, a checklist of documents to gather, or guidance on next steps — the output format changes what research is needed.
Whether the user is employed remotely, self-employed, retired, or seeking local work determines which visa categories are legally available to them.
Moving alone versus with a spouse, children, or dependents affects visa complexity, additional documentation, and whether family reunification steps are needed.
The user may want to simply understand their options at a high level, or they may want to be ready to submit an actual application — the depth of research required differs greatly.

gold.taskTitle: Research visa options for moving to Portugal
gold.taskDescription: Identify and document the relevant Portuguese visa requirements based on the user's personal situation, intended lifestyle, and timeline.

questions.title: What is your current nationality or citizenship?
questions.description: EU/EEA citizens have automatic freedom of movement to Portugal; non-EU citizens must apply for a specific long-stay visa. The answer immediately filters the entire visa landscape.

questions.title: What will your main activity be in Portugal?
questions.description: Working remotely, retiring on passive income, starting a business, studying, or seeking local employment each map to a different visa category (D7, Digital Nomad, D2, student, etc.).

questions.title: When are you aiming to make the move?
questions.description: The target timeline determines urgency, which affects whether processing times are a hard constraint and whether time-sensitive programs are still viable options.

questions.title: Will you be moving alone or with family members?
questions.description: Bringing a spouse, children, or other dependents adds family reunification steps, extra documentation requirements, and may affect visa type selection.

questions.title: Do you have a budget limit relevant to visa or relocation costs?
questions.description: Some routes (e.g. Golden Visa) require significant capital investment, while others like the D7 require proof of minimum passive income — financial constraints narrow the realistic options.

questions.title: What format do you want the research delivered in?
questions.description: The user may need a high-level options overview, a side-by-side comparison table, a step-by-step document checklist, or a recommended single path — the format shapes the depth and structure of research.

questions.title: What does a successful outcome of this research look like?
questions.description: Knowing whether the goal is general awareness, a shortlisted visa type, or full readiness to submit an application determines how deep and actionable the research needs to be.
